title: Validate ingestion and preserve rejected-record evidence
outcome: Validate a small ingestion boundary without silently coercing, dropping or repairing invalid records.
mechanism:
An ingestion boundary turns external representations into an analytical table. A successful file read only establishes that the bytes were parsed; it does not establish valid identifiers, ranges, dates or relationships. Separate structural validation from record-level admission. A missing required column can invalidate the entire batch, while an invalid measurement might be quarantined under a documented policy.

Reason codes make rejection auditable. A row with a missing ID and a negative amount may violate more than one rule. Retain all relevant flags or state a deliberate precedence for the reported primary reason. Do not let the arbitrary order of if statements become an undocumented data-quality policy.

Coercion is not repair. Turning a malformed numeric string into NA, then replacing NA with zero, creates a measured value the source never supplied. Preserve the original field and parse status where debugging requires them. A rejection report can retain only the bounded synthetic fields necessary for the lesson; a real system should also apply its privacy and retention policy.

Admission counts should reconcile. Input rows equal admitted plus quarantined rows when the sets are disjoint and exhaustive. That invariant catches accidental loss or duplication. Batch validity is still scoped to the implemented rules: a table can satisfy local range checks and remain biased, stale or scientifically unsuitable. Validation is one layer of evidence, not a guarantee of truth.

vocabulary.definition: An explicit predicate describing an admissible record.
A retained diagnostic set of records that fail admission.
A stable explanation of a validation failure.
An unexpected change in fields, types or meaning.

anatomy: Build separate logical rule flags, then a complete admitted mask. Return data and diagnostics as named fields. Require declared column names/types before evaluating row expressions, and check the input=admitted+rejected reconciliation.

worked_examples.title: Retain multiple failure flags
worked_examples.code:
raw <- data.frame(id = c("A", "", "C", "D"), amount = c(2, 3, -1, NA_real_))
flags <- data.frame(missing_id = is.na(raw$id) | raw$id == "", invalid_amount = !is.finite(raw$amount) | raw$amount < 0)
admitted <- !flags$missing_id & !flags$invalid_amount
stopifnot(identical(admitted, c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE)))
stopifnot(sum(admitted) + sum(!admitted) == nrow(raw))
print(cbind(raw, flags))
worked_examples.explanation: The negative and missing amounts remain distinct original inputs, even though both violate the same finite-nonnegative amount rule.
worked_examples.expected: One admitted row, three rejected rows.

worked_examples.title: A structural error rejects the batch
worked_examples.explanation: The validator does not silently rename an unexpected field or guess that value must mean amount. Structural drift gets an explicit failure.

exercises.prompt: Count admitted records in the first example.
exercises.hint: Every rule must pass for admission.

exercises.prompt: Return admitted and quarantined tables with stable IDs.

exercises.hint: An unparseable value is not a measured zero.
exercises.answer: Preserve a parse-failure signal and apply an explicit admission policy.

exercises.answer: Range and schema checks do not establish representativeness, causality, freshness or measurement accuracy.

reference:
validate <- function(data) {
  stopifnot(all(c("id", "amount") %in% names(data)), is.character(data$id), is.numeric(data$amount))
  flags <- data.frame(missing_id = is.na(data$id) | data$id == "", invalid_amount = !is.finite(data$amount) | data$amount < 0)
  keep <- !flags$missing_id & !flags$invalid_amount
  list(admitted = data[keep, , drop = FALSE], rejected = cbind(data[!keep, , drop = FALSE], flags[!keep, , drop = FALSE]))
}
raw <- data.frame(id = c("A", "", "C", "D"), amount = c(2, -3, -1, NA_real_))
result <- validate(raw)
stopifnot(nrow(result$admitted) == 1L, nrow(result$rejected) == 3L)
stopifnot(result$rejected$missing_id[[1]], result$rejected$invalid_amount[[1]])
stopifnot(nrow(result$admitted) + nrow(result$rejected) == nrow(raw))
empty <- validate(raw[integer(0), , drop = FALSE])
stopifnot(nrow(empty$admitted) == 0L, nrow(empty$rejected) == 0L)
cat("r-035 reference checks passed\n")
